title: LLMs struggle to simulate human belief updates in controlled environments
abstract: arXiv:2607.28347v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: LLMs are increasingly deployed as proxies for human study participants in social science experiments, yet the fidelity of this practice has rarely been tested directly. We test whether six LLMs can simulate individual human belief updates, comparing LLM outputs 1-to-1 against ground truth data from 391 UK participants on Prolific, who updated their stances on three discussion topics after reading Reddit comments. Each participant was simulated by an LLM conditioned on a persona derived from their demographic and personality trait data. Given participants' actual initial stances, five of the six models showed no systematic directional bias in their simulated post-stances, although the size of their individual-level errors varied considerably between models. All six models fail to simulate initial stances themselves and to produce faithful belief updates from self-generated stances. Three systematic biases emerge across all models: ove

translated_title: 大语言模型在受控环境中难以模拟人类信念更新
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLMs）在社会科学实验中越来越多地被用作人类研究参与者的替代者，但这种做法的忠实度却很少被直接检验。我们测试了六个大语言模型能否模拟个体人类的信念更新，将LLM的输出与来自Prolific平台上391名英国参与者的真实数据进行一对一比较，这些参与者在阅读Reddit评论后更新了他们对三个讨论话题的立场。每个参与者由一个基于其人口统计学和性格特质数据构建的人设（persona）所条件化的LLM进行模拟。在给定参与者真实初始立场的情况下，六个模型中有五个在模拟的后续立场中没有表现出系统性的方向偏差，尽管各模型之间个体层面的误差大小差异很大。然而，所有六个模型都无法模拟参与者的初始立场本身，也无法在自我生成的立场上产生忠实的信念更新。所有模型中出现了三种系统性偏差：ove（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究将六个大语言模型与391名真实参与者的信念更新数据进行一对一对比，发现尽管LLM在给定真实初始立场时无系统性方向偏差，但所有模型均无法模拟初始立场、无法产生忠实的信念更新，且存在三种系统性偏差，表明LLM作为社会科学研究中人类被试替代品的可靠性存疑。
en_tdlr: By comparing six LLMs one-to-one against ground truth belief updates from 391 human participants, this study finds that while LLMs show no systematic directional bias when given actual initial stances, all models fail to simulate initial stances and produce faithful belief updates, exhibiting three systematic biases—casting doubt on the reliability of LLMs as proxies for human participants in social science research.
